story: Launched in 1977 aboard a Titan rocket, NASA's Voyager 1 set off from Earth on a legendary journey across the Solar System. Built by the Jet Propulsion Laboratory and powered by nuclear plutonium generators, the probe performed stunning flybys of Jupiter and Saturn. It captured active volcanoes spewing on Jupiter's moon Io, investigated the dense atmosphere of Saturn's moon Titan, and carried a gold-plated record designed to tell Earth's story to alien civilizations. In August 2012, Voyager 1 became the first human-made object to cross the heliopause and enter interstellar space. To keep communicating across billions of miles via NASA's Deep Space Network, engineers have performed unbelievable remote repairs—including firing backup thrusters in 2017 after 37 years of disuse. Drifting through deep space, Voyager 1 remains humanity's farthest ambassador among the stars.
angle: In 2017, NASA engineers successfully fired Voyager 1's backup orientation thrusters after they sat completely unused in deep space for 37 years.

claims.claim: Voyager 1 was launched alongside a twin spacecraft, Voyager 2.
Voyager 1 was launched into space aboard a Titan rocket.
Voyager 1 was built and operated by NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory.
Voyager 1 conducted scientific flybys of both Jupiter and Saturn.
Voyager 1 discovered active volcanic activity on Jupiter's moon Io.
Voyager 1 made a close flyby to study the thick atmosphere of Saturn's moon Titan.
Voyager 1 carries a gold-plated phonograph disc known as the Golden Record containing Earth sounds and images for extraterrestrials.
Voyager 1 crossed the heliopause and entered interstellar space in August 2012.
Voyager 1 is powered by radioisotope thermoelectric generators using plutonium-238 fuel.
Voyager 1 transmits data to Earth using NASA's Deep Space Network.
In November 2017, engineers successfully fired Voyager 1's backup trajectory correction maneuver thrusters after 37 years of non-use.
Dr. Ed Stone served as the project scientist for the Voyager mission.
Suzanne Dodd served as the project manager for the Voyager mission.

disputed: Timing of interstellar boundary crossing determination: Scientists initially debated whether Voyager 1 crossed in late 2012 or early 2013 due to missing direct magnetic field changes, but eventually confirmed August 25, 2012 after analyzing plasma wave density oscillations triggered by solar coronal mass ejections; script should attribute the date as officially confirmed by NASA after plasma wave data review.
